description: Improve task estimates with evidence-based developer baselines, actor-aware AI-vs-human timing, and transparent calibration metadata.

userStories.title: Add estimation domain types and calibrated constants
userStories.description: As an OpenClaw tool maintainer, I want typed task-detail and actor-profile inputs so that estimates can represent human, AI-assisted, and AI-agent software work explicitly.
acceptanceCriteria: Add exported actor-profile and software-task-detail types in src/types.ts without changing existing TaskCategory or TaskComplexity literal values
Extend DurationEstimate with optional baseline metadata including actor profile, baseline source, calibration method, and adjustment factors
Add calibrated software-development baseline constants in src/constants.ts while preserving BASE_DURATION_MS for backward compatibility
Baseline constants include at least human, ai-assisted-human, and ai-agent profiles for coding, testing, debugging, documentation, and review-like work
Type-check passes
Tests pass
userStories.technicalNotes: Modify src/types.ts:31 for estimation types and src/constants.ts:20/src/constants.ts:29 for centralized constants. Follow the existing Record<TaskComplexity, number> pattern from COMPLEXITY_MULTIPLIERS and do not remove BASE_DURATION_MS because TaskTimeEstimator.getBaseline currently depends on it at src/engines/task-estimator.ts:72.

userStories.title: Apply actor-aware baseline calculation in the estimator
userStories.description: As a developer asking for an estimate, I want the estimator to account for whether a human or AI agent is doing the work so that generated timings match the actual workflow.
acceptanceCriteria: TaskTimeEstimator.estimate accepts an optional task-detail object while existing two-argument calls still compile and behave compatibly
For coding tasks with no learned baseline, expectedMs is derived from calibrated software baselines when task details identify a software task
AI-agent estimates include verification overhead rather than applying a pure line-generation speedup
Learned baselines with confidence greater than the existing 0.5 threshold continue to override default baselines
minimumMs is never greater than expectedMs and maximumMs is never less than expectedMs
Type-check passes
Tests pass
userStories.technicalNotes: Modify src/engines/task-estimator.ts:64 and src/engines/task-estimator.ts:82. Keep initializeBaselines and completeTask behavior intact at src/engines/task-estimator.ts:39 and src/engines/task-estimator.ts:151. Use calculateVariance from src/utils/confidence.ts:98 for range construction unless a task-detail-specific variance override is introduced.

userStories.title: Expose task-detail inputs through temporal tools
userStories.description: As an agent using temporal tools, I want to pass actor profile and task details to temporal_estimate and scheduling so that planning calls use the richer estimator.
acceptanceCriteria: temporal_estimate schema includes optional actorProfile, softwareTaskType, expectedFiles, expectedLinesChanged, verificationLevel, and familiarity fields
temporal_estimate passes the optional task detail object into TaskTimeEstimator.estimate
temporal_schedule_task accepts the same optional estimation fields and uses them when computing estimatedDuration
Existing calls with only category and complexity still return a valid DurationEstimate
Unsupported enum values are rejected by the tool parameter schema
Type-check passes
Tests pass
userStories.technicalNotes: Modify src/tools/temporal-tools.ts:34 to add enums beside TASK_CATEGORIES/TASK_COMPLEXITIES, src/tools/temporal-tools.ts:51 for temporal_estimate parameters, and src/tools/temporal-tools.ts:109 for temporal_schedule_task parameters. Preserve current error shape such as { error: 'Task estimator not available' } at src/tools/temporal-tools.ts:64.

userStories.title: Add focused estimator tests and package scripts
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want repeatable tests for the new estimation math so that future changes do not regress timing accuracy or compatibility.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a test runner script to package.json so bun run test executes the new test suite
Add a type-check script to package.json that runs the existing TypeScript compiler
Tests cover default compatibility for category-plus-complexity estimates
Tests cover actor ordering for the same software task: ai-agent expectedMs is less than human expectedMs for simple implementation with normal verification
Tests cover verification overhead increasing ai-agent expectedMs when verificationLevel increases
Tests cover learned baseline override when history confidence is above threshold
Type-check passes
Tests pass
userStories.technicalNotes: package.json:12 currently has only build/prepublishOnly/postinstall scripts, so add minimal scripts without disrupting npm build. There are no existing test files found under the repository root, so create a small focused suite near the estimator or under a conventional tests directory. Directly instantiate TaskTimeEstimator with TemporalCognitionState matching src/types.ts:189.

userStories.title: Document evidence-based estimation behavior
userStories.description: As a user of the temporal cognition plugin, I want docs explaining the new estimate fields and baseline caveats so that I know how to interpret AI-vs-human timings.
acceptanceCriteria: README Available Tools table keeps temporal_estimate and temporal_schedule_task descriptions accurate
README Task Estimator configuration section documents any new config options or states that no new config is required
README usage examples include an actor-aware coding estimate example
Documentation explains that AI-agent estimates include verification overhead and are not raw code-generation speed
Documentation references the package's learning behavior where actual completions can override defaults over time
Type-check passes
Tests pass
userStories.technicalNotes: Update README.md:85 for tool descriptions, README.md:129 for Task Estimator config, and README.md:216 for How It Works. Mirror the existing concise table and example style rather than adding a separate long research appendix.
